OFT.excerpt: The paper further introduces COFT (Constrained OFT), which pairs the orthogonality constraint with an explicit bound on how far the orthogonal transform may deviate from the identity, and a re-scaled variant that also learns per-neuron magnitude scalings.

OFT.probe: In the paper 'Controlling Text-to-Image Diffusion by Orthogonal Finetuning', the mathematical property of orthogonal transformations that ensures hyperspherical similarities remain unchanged is the preservation of pairwise inner products
OFT.excerpt: A crucial mathematical fact that the paper leverages is that hyperspherical energy is invariant to orthogonal transformations applied uniformly to all neurons in a layer. If $\mathbf{R}$ is orthogonal ($\mathbf{R}^\top\mathbf{R}=\mathbf{I}$) and $\mathbf{W} = \mathbf{R}\mathbf{W}^0$, then the normalized columns of $\mathbf{W}$ are rotated versions of those of $\mathbf{W}^0$, and therefore $\mathrm{HE}(\mathbf{W}) = \mathrm{HE}(\mathbf{W}^0)$.

OFT.probe: In the paper 'Controlling Text-to-Image Diffusion by Orthogonal Finetuning', the authors explain that applying the same orthogonal transformation to all neurons in a layer preserves pairwise neuron angles; if each neuron instead received a different orthogonal transformation, the expected outcome is that the pairwise neuron angles are not preserved
OFT.excerpt: A central, provable invariance exploited by OFT is that applying the same orthogonal matrix R to all neurons preserves all pairwise inner products and hence preserves HE.
